the development and application of mathematical and computational methods for modeling, analyzing and optimizing the behavior of complex biological systems.
the development of efficient and flexible tools for large-scale flux variability analyses.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

VFFVA is the first pure C implementation of flux variability analysis that relies on a hybrid MPI/Open MP management of parallelism, allowing to gain a three-fold speedup factor and a 14-fold decrease in memory usage.
we have developed a fast and memory-efficient C implementation of FBA and FVA.

the VFFVA implementation allows to gain substantial speedup and to decrease memory requirements for FVA of a large number of GSMM, which is essential for the analysis of large scale metabolic networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a pure C implementation is a better choice than a hybrid implementation in order to achieve a higher speedup factor and a better memory usage.
a careful implementation of parallelism can lead to a substantial speedup of the FVA method.

a pure C implementation, with lower level parallelism management, is more flexible and can be adapted to any type of GSMM, while the MATLAB implementation, although more user-friendly, is limited in its applicability.
